business_domains.description: This domain handles all aspects of user account lifecycle, including user registration (creating new accounts), authentication (sign-on and sign-off), and profile management (editing personal information, language preferences, favorite category, banner options). It encompasses the management of user identity and credentials. The domain maintains user personal details such as name, email, address, phone, and account-specific preferences. It interacts with database tables for account data, sign-on credentials, user profile settings, and banner display preferences. The bounded context covers everything related to a user's identity, authentication state, and stored preferences within the application.

This domain manages the product catalog that customers browse and search. It encompasses a hierarchical structure: categories (top-level groupings of pets/products), products (specific product lines within a category), and items (specific purchasable variants of a product with pricing, supplier, and attributes). The domain handles catalog browsing by category, product detail viewing, item detail viewing, keyword-based product search, and inventory availability checking. It manages inventory quantities and supplier associations for items. The bounded context covers all functionality related to presenting the store's offerings to customers, from high-level category navigation down to individual purchasable item details and stock status.

This domain manages the transient shopping cart experience for users before they commit to purchasing. It handles adding items to the cart (with stock availability checks), removing items from the cart, updating item quantities, and calculating cart subtotals. The cart is session-scoped, meaning it persists for the duration of a user's browsing session but is not permanently stored in the database. The domain manages cart items which wrap catalog items with quantity and stock status information. It provides the checkout transition point where a filled cart is handed off to the order placement process. The bounded context covers temporary item collection, quantity management, and subtotal calculation prior to order submission.

This domain manages the complete order lifecycle from placement through fulfillment tracking. It handles creating new orders (initialized from a user's account and cart contents), persisting order details including shipping and billing addresses, payment information (credit card type, number, expiry), and line items. It manages order status tracking, retrieves order history by user, and updates inventory quantities when orders are placed. The domain also handles unique order ID generation via a sequence mechanism. Order line items represent individual purchased items with quantity and price at time of purchase. The bounded context covers all aspects of purchase commitment, order persistence, order status management, and the relationship between orders and their constituent items.
